key_insight: SOTAlign frames cross-modal alignment as an optimal transport problem and uses semi-supervised OT-based matching to align frozen vision and language models, achieving strong alignment with far fewer paired examples than contrastive methods.
problem_solved: Reduces dependence on millions of labeled image–text pairs and heavy contrastive training to align pretrained unimodal vision and language models, enabling effective alignment with limited supervision and frozen backbones.
method: Formulate alignment as an optimal transport (OT) problem between sets of vision and language embeddings and compute a transport coupling (e.g., Sinkhorn) to match modalities.
Train lightweight alignment/mapping layers semi-supervisedly: a small number of labeled pairs supervise the OT coupling while large unlabeled sets inform global matching and consistency.
Keep pretrained unimodal encoders frozen to preserve representations and minimize training cost; only optimize small alignment modules for downstream cross-modal tasks.
impact: Allows practitioners to build aligned multimodal systems with much lower annotation and compute cost, improving sample efficiency for cross-modal retrieval, zero-shot transfer, and modular model reuse.

paper_title: SOTAlign: Semi-Supervised Alignment of Unimodal Vision and Language Models via Optimal Transport
paper_authors: Simon Roschmann, Paul Krzakala, Sonia Mazelet, Quentin Bouniot, Zeynep Akata
